June 14, 1978
PRIVACY AND SECRECY
My very beloved friends, you are blessed, once again.  The streamings of golden rays are
around you and fill your very being.  In this last lecture of the year, I want to give you yet another
outline of divine living, a vision of the Christ consciousness that heals all the wounds of division,
confusion, and unnecessary conflict.  You may sense that the series of lectures I have given you this
past working season was geared to give you such new visions in several respects.  These visions will
also set the pace and the climate of the work we shall be doing in the next working season.
The particular sequence of lectures may appear, off hand, arbitrary and not necessarily
connected, but upon more profound reflection, you will see that there is a meaningful sequence and
connection between the topics.  In fact, one could not be properly assimilated without the other.  All
of them form one comprehensive whole.  A study in meditation will reveal how all these topics are
intricately connected.  Every single one of the topics, and all of them together, will open new
channels of consciousness in you which, in turn, will make you capable of living the new life that is
preparing to evolve on your earth sphere.
In this topic I wish to explore the two concepts of privacy and secrecy.  There exists much
confusion about these two concepts, a confusion which fosters the aim of the forces of evil and
which prevents man from true expansion and from fulfilling all his needs.  This confusion also
makes closeness and intimacy impossible, which is surely one of man's legitimate needs.  Another is
his need for privacy.  If privacy and secrecy are being confused, either the need for closeness, or the
need for privacy with its many important aspects, must be shortchanged.
So let us now examine the difference between these two concepts.  Let us clearly understand
what each means, contains, and what its ramifications are.  Privacy is a legitimate need of the soul.
You need to be by and with yourself.  You need time alone in which you can delve into your depths
and find new levels of inner reality, undisturbed by influences and vibrations from others, even the
most favorable.  You need at times even periods in which what you essentially desire to share with
all your loved ones needs to be kept for yourself until it ripens sufficiently for sharing.  It needs time
to complete itself whether this be a thought, a new state of consciousness, an artistic creation.
Such periods of privacy do not mean isolation or separateness.  They merely indicate a
necessary state of aloneness, of being by yourself to find more of yourself.  The problem is always
that every divine reality also has a distorted, diabolic counterpart.  If privacy is being sought in order
to avoid contact, it is such a distortion.  If privacy is being avoided because the anxiety it may at first
produce is not explored and understood as to its true meaning, then it is, again, a distortion.
Many individuals are completely oblivious of the fact that they neglect their need for privacy.
They may, at times, be alone as result of circumstances beyond their control.  But even then, they

Pathwork Guide Lecture No. 252 (An Unedited Lecture)
Page 2 of 10
manage to clutter up their inner being with surface thought material, with outer or inner noise, so as
to avoid this deep inner contact for which the soul craves.  Human beings who live in perpetually
crowded conditions may have produced these very conditions because they desire an outer "reason"
for being prevented from being alone.  But by the same token, it may be equally true that human
beings live in such crowded conditions, but somehow they manage inner, and occasionally even
outer, privacy in the midst of all the busyness that surrounds them.
It is also true that those who are predominantly by themselves may have created these
conditions because of their fear of contact.  But if fear of contact exists at all, it is primarily fear of
contact with self and secondarily contact with others.  Consequently their aloneness will not fill their
need for privacy.  As mentioned, they will be alone without making use of the opportunity, just as
they will be with others without making use of the opportunity to forge true contact and intimacy.
Now what about secrecy?  Secrecy is never positive, at least not in its real sense.  We are not
talking of the so -called "secret" one keeps to prepare a lovely surprise for a loved one.  This is not
really a secret, for it is finally revealed as a joyful occasion.  Secrets always hide something negative ,
otherwise they would not be kept secret.  This is very important to realize.  Although it is quite
obvious and not at all obscure or subtle or difficult to recognize, it is surprising how often this fact
is totally overlooked.  Whatever the secret may be that you wish to keep from another or others, if
you look closer it will not be difficult to discern that you wish to hide something that is not palatable
for someone.  Either it is you who wishes something hidden from others, or another person wishes
to involve you into keeping something negative or destructive hidden.  If these hidden things -- the
secrets -- were revealed, they could be dealt with, they could be totally dissolved so that a beautiful
positive creation could take their place.  But by keeping the secret; negative thoughts, dishonest
actions, maligning, destructive behavior patterns are being maintained and continually being
nurtured.
The person who has a stake in keeping something secret -- either by himself or in conjunction
with another person or other persons -- is perfectly well aware of the fact that it is something
negative; otherwise he would not need in the least to keep this secret, whatever it may be.  To plead
righteousness about the keeping of a secret is therefore absurd.  But what usually happens is that
privacy is being used to camouflage the intent to keep secrets.  In other words, the secretive person
will use his right and need for privacy in order to conceal that he really keeps something secret.
Thus the weapon of the forces of darkness is always to confuse and use a truth to cover up a lie.
Privacy never intends to keep secrets.  In fact, just the opposite is true.  What ripens in privacy
is, when divinely inspired, later always shared with others and given on to them.  It is never meant to
hide anything.  Only dishonesty, lies, negative intentionality, destructiveness in one way or another,
needs to be hidden from others.  Nothing that is true and beautiful needs to be kept secret -- not
ever.
Sometimes the excuse "I will not be understood" or "I will be unjustly criticized" is used as a
rationalization for keeping secrets.  Again this is not valid.  For if one is in truth, understanding from
others will not be such a great necessity as to create impenetrable walls between the self and others.
If one is in truth, one makes the effort to make them understand and to work with their criticism as
a further tool to explore the reality of the situation one feels inclined to keep secret.

Pathwork Guide Lecture No. 252 (An Unedited Lecture)
Page 3 of 10
He who keeps a secret fears not being in truth, or he even knows he is not being in truth but
he has no intention whatever to change this fact.  In that way he is dishonest because he knows that
the other person may react to this fact, but he wishes to avoid this.  In other words, he wishes the
respect and love that he may not be able to earn if the secret were disclosed.
Keeping secrets is therefore always, in the final analysis, a theft.  It is a cheating action that
wants a result that cannot or may not come about if the secret were disclosed.  Keeping secrets also
means to avoid effort and responsibility to find an equitable, honest, and truthful solution in which
the other or others can participate.
Secrets are always an antithesis to relationship, to intimacy, to real and fulfilling contact.  The
secretive person is never emotionally fulfilled.  He keeps a wall of separation between himself and
others and then wonders why he feels so alone and misunderstood.  It never occurs to him to put
two and two together.  He even often blames others for his state and uses this to justify his
secretiveness instead of doing the only valid, meaningful, and intelligent thing: to spill out all secrets
and make himself as transparent as is possible.  This is not an easy or quick thing to achieve.  It
requires patience, time, effort, and all the good will that can be mastered.
Often an important reason for secretiveness is the fear of self -exposure.  The fear says "If I
show myself how I really am, they will not love me."  In this reasoning, if it can be called that,
certain blatant facts are being ignored.  For instance, it is assumed that the love, respect, or approval
of others is more important than one's own.  It is being ignored that the courage and honesty of
transparency, no matter what shameful facets may have to be revealed, creates at first more
self-esteem than the secretiveness ever could.  And therefore eventually it must also create esteem
and love from others.
This path is blatantly designed to gradually but surely eliminate all secrets.  First you learn to
no longer have secrets from yourself.  You experience that there exists a great deal of material that
you had ignored, that was unconscious, that is secret from your conscious mind.  Then, this same
honesty and openness you have acquired toward yourself, you learn to apply it also to others.  If you
go steadily that way, you cannot help experience that this is the only way to be, to exist.  It is the
only way your need for contact can be fulfilled.  The only way you can live without fear and anxiety,
without shame and hiding, without pretenses and facades.  The relief of this kind of living is a much
headier wine than any pseudosolution could ever be.  Those who have begun to taste it can no
longer stand for long to revert back to secret living in any area or respect, no matter what may come
up.
If you have negative thoughts about others, suspicious opinions or accusations, instead of
nurturing them secretly for yourself or sharing them with a third person as a mutually kept secret,
you will bring it all out into the open.  Doing so indicates that your will to be in truth is greater than
your negative opinion, your accusations, your suspicions.  You will proceed into a journey within the
great journey of life to explore what the particular truth of this situation is.  You cannot fail to be
enlightened with the real, peace -bringing, unifying truth if you are committed to it more than to
anything else.  Wanting to preserve your secret, on the other hand, indicates clearly that you have no
commitment to the truth -- probably not even to the truth that you have a stake in -- and that you
have a desire for maintaining your negative opinions, accusations, and suspicions precisely because,
deep inside of you, you already know that you are not in truth but do not wish to admit this.

Pathwork Guide Lecture No. 252 (An Unedited Lecture)
Page 4 of 10
Accusations that are being made publicly do not necessarily indicate openness, a converse to
secrecy.  It may merely mean that hostile and aggressive factors supersede secrecy.
It is easy to see that the new man and the new woman are incapable of abiding secrets.  They
cannot be borne in the newly emerging consciousness.  They are experienced as an unbearable
burden, which it actually is.  The spiritual form of a secret is exactly that -- a heavy burden.  The
more enlightened conscious becomes, the more infused with the Christ spirit, the speedier the
burden will be dissolved in the most productive and creative way possible.
You have begun to experience this new mode of living in your own growing community.  This
is precisely what is taking place -- an ever increasing openness and transparency in which all secrets
of self and others are being experienced as insufferable burdens, as hindrances to light and love.
The price for keeping a secret becomes too high, too absurd.  No effort to eliminate secrets so that
the soul can stand clear and clean -- visible for all to see -- is too high.  This must be the goal.  It
applies to all manner of relationships: to man/woman partnerships, to every kind of friendship, and
finally also to the relationships between countries.
As a result of keeping negative aspects secret, it is also impossible to reveal the best of self.
One feels embarrassed about it.  Or simply one's innermost thoughts, dreams, and desires feel
shameful.  To begin with, these aspects are often far from shameful or bad.  But something in the
soul turns them negative as a result of the veil of secrecy that is being established.  The mere fact
that one believes there must be something hidden, creates an aura of fog, of darkness that gradually
encompasses the best in the person.  It is therefore essential that this fog be dissolved, whether what
is hidden is outright negative or only becomes so as a result of the hiding process.
The process of dissolving the hidden secrets consists, to a large degree, of what you already do
on this path.  You muster the courage to expose what was hitherto a secret.  In no way have you
ever had occasion to regret this step.  For always you have found more love, more respect, more
friendship, more help, more recognition of your real values, not to speak of the relief of losing an
unbearable burden.  The clarity, the sense of liberation, and the heady wine of no longer pretending
in any way are the direct doorway to the self -esteem you so desperately looked for in a false way
before.
If your self-revealing seems to have elicited more criticism and censure rather than more love
and understanding, I would say to you, my friends, that your self -revealing must surely have
occurred in a distorted way.  It is easy to confuse the real way with the false one.  The real way is the
absolute willingness to follow the will of God; to let go of every cherished attitude, action, or goal if
they should prove to be damaging and counter to divine law; to use those to whom you reveal
yourself as mirrors that help you to reconsider some of your previous patterns.  Their reaction
should not be your inflexible rule that you must abide, but should make you thoughtful and truly
willing to reconsider whatever it is.
The false way of self-revealing and dissolving secrets is the childish, lower self aim that says, in
effect: "If I show you my secrets, I demand that you approve of them and of me regardless of how
destructive they may be.  If you do not, I will accuse you of letting me down and will use this as a
proof that it does not pay to be open."  So be careful, my friends, when you adjudge the results of

Pathwork Guide Lecture No. 252 (An Unedited Lecture)
Page 5 of 10
your self-revealing.  The key always lies deep within you:  are you really moved by the sincere desire
to be in truth and to do the will of God?
On the other hand, you also need to clearly understand when there exists a real violation of
your privacy.  When others try to pry, out of their own negative motives, out of a sickly kind of
curiosity that they may wish to use against you, or because they want to prove something against you
so as to make themselves feel better and to enhance their deteriorated self -value, then you should
indeed close the doors to them.  But the fact is that you can never truly recognize the distinction
between actual prying and violation of your privacy and from genuine concern for you and the
desire to relate to the real you on the part of others -- unless you are willing to give up all secrets,
unless you have already begun to do so.  As long as you harbor a stake to keep yourself hidden, your
assessment of others' motives will be very shaky and not reliable.
Self-revealing, openness, transparency is not only a new habit that needs to be acquired with
patience, devotion, and perseverance, due to recognizing its importance for you and those around
you with whom you long to relate.  It is also an art that can be, need be, learned.  Often the
hesitancy and inhibitions that exist to begin with can be removed when you learn how to express
yourself, how to convey what first seems unconveyable.  Has it not frequently occurred to you that
you relayed a dream quite adequately, once you started it, although you were first convinced it
cannot be explained?  In the four walls of your inner self, thoughts and attitudes, experiences and
feelings seem so vague, so diffused, so unexplainable that you do not even attempt to convey them.
But once you know it is possible to do so, even if not all of the shadings and nuances come out one
hundred percent correct, you will make efforts and you will be surprised to what extent you can
make yourself clear and reach others who may have quite similar inner experiences and thus can
emotionally connect with you sooner and better than you may have suspected.
The point I want to make is that communication is an essential part of self -revealing and
openness.  Effort is needed, a lot of effort, but this effort will be highly rewarded.  What first
appears to be embarrassing, only seems that way because you cannot really put it in the proper
words.  Once you try, these words will come.  A new wonderful art of self -expression and
articulateness will develop that in itself will enhance your sense of security and adequacy.  Your
initial inability to express yourself adequately is totally due to your not really wanting it and therefore
not allowing God to infill you.  The Holy Spirit will inspire you with the appropriate words, and this
will remove the walls you have built around you.
Let us examine the quality of the various human relationships in the light of this topic.  The
most intimate of all relationships -- between a man and a woman who love each other and intend to
share themselves with one another, completely -- depends on the ability to be without secrets.  Thi s
includes the outer ones as well as the inner, more subtle ones.  If the risk is not taken to bring
everything of the self into play, the bliss that is expected can never materialize.  I have discussed this
before in connection with the specific topic of the relationships between mates.  I need to repeat it
here in context with the personality's tendency to keep the self secret.  The false belief that the self is
otherwise not acceptable must be challenged again and again.  The risk needs to be taken again and
again, step by step, until all is out in the open.  Then the ongoing process of communicating the
inner processes and sharing them can begin.  Again it is not a one -time goal that is now achieved for
good.  Of course there may exist a great deal of residual material that you have accumulated.  Once
this is emptied out, and all is made known of you, the ongoing process can begin.  For the soul is

Pathwork Guide Lecture No. 252 (An Unedited Lecture)
Page 6 of 10
not a static, fixed thing.  It constantly moves and changes, forever producing new inner experiences,
new feelings, new thought material, new aims, new dreams.  But once you have emptied yourself,
the dynamic process of soul development can be shared much more easily.  The art of
communicating, of self-expression, of explaining yourself adequately grows as you g row.  Thus you
become an increasingly open channel for divine inspiration, which also affects the choice of words,
the finer shades and distinctions that seem so difficult to put into words, the tone of voice that also
contributes to making yourself clear.  Thus what was once a confined prison of your inner self
becomes a wide open field, ever more clearly available for all others, that reaches the infinite
horizons of divine possibilities.  A state of mind grows in which there is nothing to hide, in which
hiding seems utterly absurd and being totally transparent the greatest joy.
How else can you know your real value?  Only when you risk to present whatever you are
now.  In this process you will inevitably find that there is so much more to you than you feared.
How else can you find fulfillment and squelch your thirst for being open with others, for attaining
intimacy?  This longing can never be fulfilled, no matter how hard you may try to deny it or give it
pseudofulfillments.
The word friendship becomes a farce if you feel there is anything to hide between yourself
and the friend.  It is at best very limited.  And you will never really know whether you are loved and
accepted, you must always fear and distrust as long as the risk is not being taken to show the friend
all you are, all you have kept hidden.  But this of course always includes the basic willingness to
change what is a lower self act, a lower self goal, a lower self activity.  It requires the trust that higher
self goals and activities will provide you much better with what you need.  If this trust is lacking,
then this is what you need to share -- and perhaps receive help with.
The whole idea of this pathwork is obviously designed to remove the secrets and to make
yourself available.  If you look back on your progress so far, from this point of view, you will see
quite clearly that to whatever degree you have liberated yourself and improved your life
circumstances, to whatever degree you have gained new self -confidence and a sense of your own
value, to whatever degree you trust God and life more and know of divine abundance, it is due to
the courage of openness and revealing of outer and/or inner subtle secrets.  Look where you still
keep hiding, and you will find the key to where your life is still blocked from the fulfillment that is
waiting for you.
When you look at your world, at the interaction between countries, it will become apparent
how much this factor weighs.  The interrelationships between countries is more marked than any
other relationship by secretiveness, pretense, and hiding.  Openness between the governments of
different countries is not even considered as viable.  It is taken for granted by all concerned that
opaqueness is sound diplomacy.  In this area mankind is far behind where it could and should be,
and far behind the other areas of human relationships although they, too, still leave something to be
desired.  If you view the general attitudes in marriage, you will also recognize to what extent mates
keep secrets from one another -- not only about the past and the present as far as actual actions and
experiences are concerned, but also about their thoughts and feelings and inner shading of
experience.  Is it any wonder that marriage does not seem to work out very well and that mates
cannot stay together?  Yet in this respect it is so much better than in the relationship between
different governments.  And it is there that most distrust, most deceit, most strife exists.  As long as
humanity does not begin to envision an altogether new way of interrelating, peace cannot truly be

Pathwork Guide Lecture No. 252 (An Unedited Lecture)

established; sharing of the riches God has provided cannot take place; justice and brotherhood will
remain mere empty phrases.  In short, the willingness to be open must exist.  It must be recognized
that this is a prerequisite for a life of peace, joy, and harmony between all the peoples of this earth.
It must then be learned painstakingly, just as you as individuals do.
You are pioneers, bringing the new model to this world.  I have said this before, and I say it
again, this time in connection with this topic.  In establishing your community life, you encounter
basically the same problem that humanity as a whole encounters in establishing society.  You see
clearly that those who keep themselves secret, who do not share all of themselves, represent a dark
barricade that hinders the fabric of the whole.  You need to make this fact understood by those who
do not dare as yet to be real.  You need to know it for yourself.  You will learn increasingly, slowly
perhaps but yet inexorably, to present yourself in totality, without any false self -projections.  To
whatever degree you do not trust the process of a "secretless life," you must understand that you
encourage a false self -projection.  Your secrets mean ex actly that, "I want you to see me, not as I
am, but as I pretend to be."  Once you clearly see this fact, how can you imagine that this does not
have the gravest consequences on your relationship with yourself, with others, with your God?
How could this possibly not effect your entire outer and inner life and those with whom you are
involved and attempt to establish a desirable relationship?
Just imagine, try to visualize, what life is like when you know that there is nothing ever to hide.
And if you feel that there is, perhaps that which you hide is really something damaging, destructive
for yourself and/or others and should be revealed all the more because you need help in recognizing
what causes your desire for this act or attitude.  You then need help to change your inner
mechanisms so that you will no longer need to desire a destructive act or attitude.
Or perhaps what you believe should be kept hidden is really a beautiful aspect of you and
should be shared.  Or perhaps you only think it is bad and need the experience of exposing it before
you can really be convinced that you have nothing to hide.  Even that which is your lower self is not
to be hidden, so that it can be healed and transformed.  Imagine the feeling of no longer hiding
anything from anyone.  Imagine the freedom, like shedding a heavy armor.  Imagine the joy and the
good healthy pride, your head held high, your eye clear in knowing you can truly be open to all.
Only when this state of consciousness is being achieved can the true unfoldment begin.  Your
limitless potentials for greatness, for creativity, for still hidden talents, for your universality and
uniqueness, for your essence and your beauty can stream forth only when the confinement of hiding
is removed.  The process of self -unfoldment begins with removing the walls of secretiveness, the
confinement of hiding and deceiving the world about who you are now, and it continues with
liberating the best in you only after this has been accomplished.  Of course the process often
overlaps and changes back and forth.  As one layer or aspect of hiding is being dissolved, new
qualities and assets develop that you have never known.  Then you return to other areas of hiding
that you had not even been clearly aware of before, so that more of your potentials can begin to
unfold.
Can you visualize a world in which no one ever hides anything any longer from anyone else?
Is that not paradise?  This is the direction in which evolution moves, my friends.  This is what the
new age signifies.  How can Christ in you truly express through and to you if you have any hidden
agenda?  How can your divinity unfold if you are not free and if you continue to project a false self

Pathwork Guide Lecture No. 252 (An Unedited Lecture)

into the world?  Do not rationalize it by pretending it is to preserve your privacy.  Look at the real
motives, at the real reasons why you maintain this painful and unnecessary state of isolation and
deception -- for that is what it truly amounts to.
There are fundamentally three reasons for the resistance to give up your secrets: (1) the fear
that your lower self makes you all bad and your unwillingness to risk taking the chance that this is
not so, that others will not reject you nor will you find it necessary to do so yourself; (2) ignorance
that there is a way to be learned of communicating all that now seems incommunicable;
unwillingness to learn the process gradually by small steps; (3) fear of being too vulnerable when all
the hard shells fall off (and secrets are certainly one of the hardest layers).  The common
denominator of all these three factors is the resistance to go with all of yourself to God and trust His
will.  It is perpetuated by following the voices of the dark forces who inspire you to trust your false,
destructive, separating devices for safety and for the resolution of your problems.  You need to
become aware of these influences, and you desperately need to challenge them and refute them.
New choices of action, behavior, and of seeking solutions will have to be actively made by you.
Before terminating this lecture, I wish to speak more about the third factor, fear of
vulnerability.  This vulnerability goes beyond the obvious fear of being less "protected" from hurt
and disappointment.  This fear is an outright illusion and easy to discover as such, once the courage
to risk is summoned.  But there is another kind of vulnerability I wish to speak about.  As you
become more open, more accessible, more unhidden, new capacities of perception grow.  What you
perceived previously only dimly, becomes more and more acute, more clearly defined.  In many
areas of life, this is immediately and directly a tremendous asset.  The only thing is that this desirable
result is totally ignored by the personality because there is too much darkness and fog present to
know reality.  Therefore the incentive is lacking.
But there is also another effect created by this newly evolved vulnerability, that is not
immediately experienced as desirable.  It is a grieving pain about the destruction caused by evil.  It is
healthy and good when this state grows in you, when you can experience this.  It manifests in
different ways, and the more aware of it you become, the more you will experience this very healthy
pain.  You may feel a pain when you see God's gifts in nature being willfully destroyed.  You may
feel a pain about the suffering on this plane of existence.  For example, animals who need to be the
prey of other animals in order to sustain their life feel deeply that they fulfill their function.  And in
one sense this suffering is certainly much less than the suffering inflicted willfully by indifference
and cruelty from man.  Yet, the fact that they have to go through this phase of their own evolution
is painful although there is an intrinsic rightness about it.  These are incarnated aspects of
consciousness that need these experiences, but they are, nevertheless, on the level of manifestation,
much more innocent than man who has a consciousness and awareness that gives him much more
responsibility.
What I say here may sound contradictory, yet it is not.  I must ask you to try to understand
this in your depth from which a true grasping will come.  Compassion and love, gratitude for the
beauty of creation, appreciation of and joy about it must also create a deep pain that needs to be
suffered.  It is ever so different from neurotic pain, from the kind of pain by association, the pain of
masochistic self-punishment that identifies with what appears to be victims.  This living, healthy,
loving pain is also the threshold to joy and ecstasy.

Another aspect of this pain is the recognition of damage inflicted by thoughts of untruth
about your fellow human beings; thoughts of maligning and unwarranted suspicion; inner and/or
outer acts of factual, psychological, emotional, and spiritual cheating that imposes unfair
disadvantages on others even though such cheating may well be camouflaged and rationalized away
until the consciousness truly ignores it and fights with all its might against recognition.
As long as these pains are denied, the price is much higher, for it cannot help but turn against
him who inflicts these pains or who colludes with those who do by passively standing by.  Many
self-defeating patterns are never connected with pains you have unwittingly and blindly inflicted
because you have not allowed yourself to know and feel them.  It seemed too tempting to follow the
way of the dark forces and too undesirable to give them up.  But not only your own pain about this
is feared and avoided, thereby accruing into debilitating guilt and indirect self -punishment; you also
need to feel the liberating pain where it has nothing to do with you, where you simply see it existing
on this sphere and allow this experience to strengthen your determination to become an ever
stronger fighter in the legion fighting for the forces of light.
So, my beloved friends, when the walls of separation and secretiveness fall from you, you step
out into a beautiful world of light, of goodness, of singing joy, of eternal life, of fearless existence.
This world can only exist in a defenseless person, free from armoring, free from denying the soft
vulnerability that can experience all suffering created by the forces of evil.  If you harden yourself
against this kind of pain, you also deny the joy that is meant to be yours for all eternity.
The blessings of all the angels accompany you, the blessings of the Highest flows through
them to you, enriching and guiding your life.  The presence of the Highest, of the Creator, lives in
your heart and soul if you only will see and feel it.  The short period of time in which I will not give
you lectures or answer your questions will be fully utilized by all those who will wish to do so, so
that we cannot really speak of interruption.  It is simply a time of outbreathing and refueling while
your inner path progresses and assimilates.  Be always aware that you are here on this earth plane to
find your true being and fulfill for God.  Live in Him.

CONTINUE YOUR STRUGGLE AND CEASE ALL STRUGGLE
Divine and joyful blessings, my beloved friends.  Your tasks become more joyful, more
fulfilling, more noticeably meaningful.  For many of you this is so!  Your inner paths bring this outer
meaning to your life.  As your community grows, the cleansing process must be an inexorable
by-product, my beloved ones.  As you cleanse yourselves inwardly and leave behind aspects of your
personality that are not compatible with your newly awakening self, so must the entity pathwork do
the same.
So we begin a new working season.  Much expansion, excitement, fulfillment, and challenges
await you.  Even unavoidable hardship must ultimately become yet another tool for greater harmony
and ecstasy.  I wish to discuss this topic in the first lecture of your new working year.
In the great plan, also called the plan of salvation, the earth sphere is meant to gradually
change into a more spiritual abode of unity, harmony and light.  This cannot, of course, be an outer
process that is "given" from outside.  It can only come about through a transformation of
consciousness in the earth's inhabitants.  This transformation of consciousness, in turn, comes about
as a result of laborious inner work -- the work of purification, self -confrontation, and of
consequently finding new, deeper inner levels of reality hitherto disconnected from your conscious
being.  As the earth transforms, those individual consciousnesses that cannot and will not follow this
process of growth and development, create a new abode similar to the conditions that have
prevailed in this earth sphere and that are still prevailing now.  These conditions begin to change
already among a relatively small section of the earth's inhabitants.  But as time goes on, the number
will increase.  Your specific path is a potent measure to bring this change about in a minimum
amount of time.  What might otherwise take many incarnations could be accomplished in one life
time if the pathwork is truly followed to its maximum potential.  Such transformations have already
been witnessed among you and are being experienced by some of you as a strong sense of being
reborn in this very lifetime.
I would like to discuss a particular aspect of this transformation of consciousness that has
been mentioned many times before.  But here I wish to emphasize very specifically what was
previously discussed in more general ways.  Mankind's greatest imprisonment, from which all fear
and pain and suffering stem, is the duality in which the human mind is entangled.  The mass mind
then builds conditions and an environment that express this bent of consciousness.  It is perhaps the
most difficult aspect of man's evolutionary journey to penetrate the myth of this seeming reality --
the reality that the world is dualistic.
You seem to be put into an entirely objective world, all fixed and ready made.  All conditions
and natural laws seem to be unalterable givens that your state of consciousness has no influence on
whatever.  This false reality seems indeed the most "realistic" and sane acceptance of life.  And the

Pathwork Guide Lecture No. 253 (An Unedited Lecture)
Page 2 of 9
problem is that to a certain degree this is indeed so.  It is necessary to accept the world as you find it
and deal with it on its own terms.  For even after your own consciousness begins to change and
transcend, the creation of mass mind still remains intact.  In that transitional state, the individual
lives in both realities.  He fully accepts the created, dualistic reality, but recognizes simultaneously
the new vision gradually evolving through the fog.  This new vision you know about in your mind,
but a few of you have occasionally begun to experience its reality.  It is the absolute knowledge that
there is only good, that there is eternal life, peace, joy, excitement, meaning, that there is nothing to
fear, that there is no more pain.  Part of this state of ultimate reality is also the knowledge that you
create your world, your conditions, your environment; and that knowledge, rather than burdening
you, gives you an immense sense of liberation and safety.
Not accepting the conditions of this dualistic world because of the vague knowledge of
another state of mind that can be attained -- is an aberration.  It expresses the childish de sire for
omnipotence in a cheap and easy way.  It deludes itself that by an outer act of sheer will the
developmental stages -- which sometimes must include temporary suffering -- can be avoided.  Thus
we have the apparent paradox of glimpsing ultimate reality in a false way leading to more unreality
than not glimpsing it at all and fully accepting the conditions of this mass illusion.  But when the
limitations of these life conditions are being fully accepted and the personality deals with them
honestly, maturely, productively, and constructively, then the inner evolutionary process continues
organically, and the mind begins to encompass other visions that were invisible before.  To deal with
your limited reality in this way you must include a process of stringent self -work, such as this
pathwork offers you.
Progress in this inner work brings about many changes.  Changes of attitudes, changes of
intentionalities, changes of feelings, changes of opinions, changes of world view and, last but not
least, change of perceiving reality.  A very simple and current example, on a very practical level, is
what all of you continually experience on this path.  You start out seeing a certain condition in your
life in a very specific way.  Let us say you are convinced that certain circumstances victimize you;
that others are doing you a great wrong; that you have no recourse in changing these conditions,
unless these others change their attitude and behavior toward you.  Few are those who have entered
this path where some such situation has not come up.  In such a situation you start out with a very
firmly held conviction.  All aspects you can observe bear out this conviction.  In fact, the more
convinced you are, the more "proof" you will be able to collect as to how accurate your conviction
is.  This self-perpetuating vicious circle, this law that creates the vision according to your conviction,
is the ensnarlment of the mind that is so hard to overcome.
Only as a result of much good will on your part to open your mind, to let go, at least
temporarily, of your conviction will you begin to recognize new aspects that you could never see
before.  Perhaps you will see how you actively contributed to the situation that seemed to place all
the responsibility onto the other person.  You may recognize on yet deeper levels a definite
intentionality to create a negative situation.  This recognition will automatically shift the total picture.
Not that it will place all the burden of guilt now on you and necessarily make a victim out of the
previous villain, but you probably will see how you mutually affected each other.
This comprehension will open new vistas.  You will soon come to recognize entirely unsensed
aspects of yourself and the others involved -- both good and bad, favorable  and unfavorable.  But

Pathwork Guide Lecture No. 253 (An Unedited Lecture)
Page 3 of 9
underneath this duality of good versus bad one day you will find an ultimate, unchangeable level of
truth in which all is good in a new, different, more alive, and very dynamic way.
Here I used a familiar example that demonstrates the process of extending man's vision to
new realities.  In this example, you find that the previous limitation seemed indeed plausible.  You
will find that it was inaccurate mostly because of its exclusivity; because you saw it out of context
with other elements.  And without cognizance of these other elements, the total picture is distorted.
It was not false because your view is necessarily untrue in itself (although that exists too), but false
because you leave out other essential elements that are necessary in order to glimpse the total
picture.  What I am trying to convey here is that many realities exist in regard to one and the same
situation, condition, circumstance.  By knowing this, you will beware of quick evaluations but will
undertake the responsibility you carry to search, to grope, to make effort, to extend your vision.
The same process exists in regard to the world and its natural laws as you know them.  Your
world view is based on a very incomplete vision that allows only limited areas of your perception to
filter into your consciousness.  You see what appears most obvious on an entirely superficial level.
But as you grow personally, as your perception of reality of your personal circumstances widens, so
does your perception of creation begin to alter, to widen, and deepen.  You glimpse connections you
have never seen before and that are now as obvious as the limited reality you perceived before.
The dualistic world view seems an incontrovertible fact.  Not to see your world in terms of
opposites, of duality, appears the crassest form of delusion.  And it is true indeed that on the level of
appearance, duality is a fact.  Life seems to die.  Evil always lurks somewhere in the shadows no
matter how much good also exists.  Light opposes darkness.  Night opposes day.  Where there is
health there also exists sickness.  Yet, another reality awaits to be recognized underneath this level of
opposites.  Since living within the level of duality (opposites) brings pain and strain, it is the soul's
greatest longing to find this deeper level of truth.  This longing, as I often said, exists regardless of
whether or not a person is conscious of it.  It fills the heart precisely because it is within the scheme
of an individual's potential to awaken into this new level at some point of his or her evolutionary
journey.
I have talked about this before, and the reason I mention it now is because I wish to show the
way more precisely how to attain this new level of perception and of being.  It must be clearly
understood that the goal cannot be willed by the outer will alone.  It cannot come about as a result
of philosophical speculation or theoretical knowledge or even as a result of specific exercises,
methods, or disciplines.  The change of consciousness happens entirely due to an intensely personal
purification process that, to begin with, deals always with the most mundane matters of your
practical life, with your attitudes toward these matters and your general surroundings.  Practical
everyday matters are always an expression of inner, subtle, and finally spiritual attitudes.  To skip
them and consider them irrelevant only leads to further separation, duality (spirituality versus
practical life).  Therefore, ultimately this leads to a delusionary spirituality that is not grounded in the
now.  This is why you find this path so intensely practical and utterly compatible with your life of
matter, your daily activity, and your goals.  The path is not only compatible with these, but it is also
an expression of the most subtle spiritual (or anti-spiritual) attitudes.
Let us now attempt to be a little more specific about attaining the new consciousness in which
creation is no longer perceived in terms of duality.  Perhaps we should begin by pointing out how

Pathwork Guide Lecture No. 253 (An Unedited Lecture)
Page 4 of 9
painful and fearful duality really is.  For this is often so much taken for granted that you cannot even
perceive the pain and fear.  You do not know anything else.  This is all there is, so how could you
even begin to chafe under it?  It is a similar dynamic to a child's hardly feeling his painful conditions
simply because he does not know that other conditions might exist.  In order to change existing
conditions, one must feel them as so desirable that the effort is well worth taking.  But one must
also know that they can be changed, that other possibilities indeed exist.
Most human beings do not know that duality is painful, nor how painful it really is.  Nor do
they know that another way of living exists, another view of perception exists that totally eliminates
this pain.  Living trapped in the limited world of duality, there is always the fear of the undesirable --
the straining away from it and straining toward the desirable.  This very straining is extremely painful
and anxiety producing.  But this strain becomes conscious only at a point on your path after a great
deal of crude purification work has been accomplished.  If this specific strain is being dealt with
before such crude purification work -- such as you are involved with now -- important steps are
being skipped, and the process cannot take place in an organic, grounded way.  So what I shall
discuss now may not necessarily be appropriate for a number of my friends at this time, but I believe
it will help all of you to comprehend some of these aspects now, even before you are ready on your
personal path to really emphasize this new phase.  If may also facilitate your present phase if you can
connect with some of my words; and it may help you to deepen some of your present understanding
of yourself in regard to simple purification work you have been doing all along.
Obviously we are talking here about different states of mind.  If the dualistic state of mind
becomes more firmly entrenched in the painful, fearful dualism through straining from the
undesirable alternative, then it must figure that the straining must be relinquished .  Yet, how can I
say to you, do not wish for happiness as opposed to suffering; life as opposed to death; health as
opposed to illness, and so on?  You would hardly be human if you would not deeply desire
happiness, life, health.
But there is a state of mind in which the straining relaxes, in which the undesirable can be
dealt with in an almost similar spirit and attitude as the desirable.  This may appear very strange to
you now, but I truly say to you, my beloved friends, this is indeed so.  Perhaps the first step in this
particular scale is to pay attention to the by-products in your feelings, thoughts, attitudes as you
experience either a desirable or an undesirable state.  If the desirable occurs, you are probably most
likely to feel faith in the Lord, to experience His reality; you can connect with the Christ within; you
can be joyful in the knowledge that all is well in this world.  (I now address myself to individuals
who do believe in and can occasionally experience spiritual reality beyond this earth reality, and not
people who have never yet experienced this level of being).  But it is infinitely more difficult to
maintain the same faith, the same knowing, when the undesirable experiences occur.  The feelings
immediately fluctuate like the needle in a compass.  Just begin to observe your moods.  When are
doubts coming up?  What brings on these doubts?  Is it not always in some way connected with
whether or not the desirable goal occurs?
The Christed person does not experience these fluctuations.  The outer experience in no way
influences which level of reality he is connected with.  It is indeed true that such a person reacts to
pain in no way differently than he reacts to pleasure.  In that way they become indeed one and the
same.  To put it differently, duality is being transcended.

Pathwork Guide Lecture No. 253 (An Unedited Lecture)
Page 5 of 9
This kind of detachment is strongly fostered by Eastern religions, as well as by the Western
mystics.  It explains why these disciplines negate worldly fulfillment and consider them an antithesis
to the goal of spiritual self -realization.  It explains all the disciplines of asceticism and deliberately
imposed suffering.  Yet, valuable as these approaches may be to a degree, does not the deliberate
negation of the desirable lead to a similar state of duality, only approached from the other end?  He
who denies the undesirable is not much different from him who denies the desirable, who does not
permit himself to rejoice in it!
Also there seems to exist another kind of contradiction that has led to many confusions in the
human mind and in the spiritual aspirants.  Is it not also claimed by spiritual teachers and seers that
God's will is your happiness, your human fulfillment, your health, your well being, your healing
when you are ill, your productivity and success in life?  So how then can you negate this life here and
now that the Creator has given you?  Does it seem right to abdicate all material existence and deny
its desirable aspects because you know that there exists a yet deeper, much more permanent state of
mind in which you can experience life and fulfillment without the breaks that are part and parcel of
the dualistic state of mind?
All these questions seem fraught with conflict and contradiction -- at least on this level of
reality.  In a deeper sense there are no contradictions at all.  It is utterly possible to rejoice in worldly
fulfillments as expressions of inner states, while no longer straining toward one state and away from
another.  This latter attitude can exist only when you deeply know that ultimately there is the reality
of God; there is life eternal; and there is fulfillment and well being in every possible way.  Because
you have attained a state without straining, you glimpse and finally experience this other reality.  It is
equally true to state that you can relinquish the straining because you glimpse this state.  It must be
approached from both ends.
It would be virtually impossible to start out with an attempt to feel the same way about two
opposites.  You could not possibly make yourself react the same way to pleasure as to pain.  It is a
natural movement of the human manifestation to strain toward pleasure and away from pain.  Even
the often encountered fear of and denial of pleasure is essentially nothing but another version of fear
and denial of pain.  So how then is one to start in this particular direction, you may well ask.  As
long as the strain between two opposites of a duality exists, you must live in fear, in inner tension;
and you cannot realize your ultimate state of unity in which there is no death and no pain.
The way to go about it at first is to stand back and truly observe your reactions to pain and
pleasure, to life and death.  These reactions contain a great deal of material that you need to become
quite clear about but that you generally ignore.  These reactions have become so much second
nature to you that you cannot see the forest for the trees.  Fear and desire are only the most
common denominators that designate a host of other feelings and attitudes.  In your fear of death
and of pain and in your movement to strain away from them, there is usually contained a great deal
of anger, bitterness, and resentments.  It is not toward a specific person or deity.  It is a more
general, diffuse, but nevertheless quite distinct, state of mind.  Many times these feelings of
bitterness and anger become enmeshed into the system that they themselves turn into the pain that
is so rejected.  In other words, what started out as a small pain manifestation and what might
dissolve smoothly and relatively soon, becomes more firmly entrenched and aggravated.  It is, once
again, not so much these anger feelings themselves as their suppression and repression.  The fact
that you are unaware of them and that they can therefore exist underground has the damaging effect.

Pathwork Guide Lecture No. 253 (An Unedited Lecture)
Page 6 of 9
You therefore need to make these reactions very clear and conscious.  This is in a certain way more
difficult than with specifically directed anger feelings toward specific individuals and specific events.
The latter may contradict your idealized self -image, your moral standards, your overall personality,
but the former anger is so irrational and unreasonable seeming that the ordinary person fears
insanity if he riles against what life is known to be.  How can you "reasonably" resent the existence
of death?  How can you be angry about it?  How can you even be angry that you, like all other
humans, fall occasionally ill and suffer pains?  Yet there exists a rage toward life and creation in all
human souls before realization of the unitive, deathless, painless state has been attained.  The feeling
is, if it were articulated: how can life (God) be so cruel as to impose an inevitable event at the end of
one's existence that is unfathomable, that is totally unknown, that is deeply threatening because it
may be the end of one's existing, of one's being.  No matter how certain individuals who have to
come to embrace atheism claim to have accepted to no longer exist, in this very "acceptance" lies the
ultimate of rage.  Atheism itself is a manifestation of extreme bitterness against a creation that seems
so utterly senseless and arbitrary that no recourse exists.  Atheism is the movement that cuts off all
sensibilities and sensitivities which might open up the perception of deeper and different realities.
There can never be a genuine "acceptance" of ending one's being.  Such false acceptance is
always either an angry bitter resignation or despair with life and its pains.  At the same time,
accepting eternal life can also come from identical reasons of fear.  So you need to go through your
inner fear and your previously unconscious anger, bitterness, or rage at life for imposing death and
pain on you, for putting you in a position in which you find yourself helpless against these common
human experiences.  As you become aware of these feelings and accept their apparent
unreasonableness and childishness, you will then be able to make new connections.  You will see
how the unrecognized feelings have channeled themselves, in what particular way they have found
expression.  And since this kind of deflection can never lead to clarity and truth, to harmony and
unity, the deflection leads you further away from the fulfillment of your soul's longing -- namely the
real inner knowing of the unitive state.  Thus, the less aware you are of what you feel about these
very general existential matters of life, the more irrational these feelings will become.  The less you
can permit yourself to face them (or so you believe), the more deflected they will be, and the deeper
you become ensnarled in the dualistic state with all its painful strains and anxieties.  The denied fear
creates more fear.  The denied longing and desire create anxiety, not peace.  Only the courage to go
through these feelings will purify them as the gold emerges in the hands of the alchemist.  Both the
fear and the desire will become the driving force, in a most positive sense, to find your longing, to
find that in this longing exists a kernel of true knowing that it can find fulfillment.
From this stage slowly comes and with many interruptions at first, a state in which you want
life, not because you fear death, but because you know that there is no death.  You know that
leaving the body brings a better life.  These words have often been spoken, but they are rarely
experienced as inner truth.  To do so, a specific approach on your path, such as I outline here, must
be pursued.  There is a vast difference between hanging on to life because you fear annihilation of all
you are, of who you have become, and between affirming life because you cherish the task your life
on earth means.  You rejoice in bringing parts of the greater, real life into this dualistic plane and to
thus spiritualize the matter you temporarily inhabit.
The same applies to pain and painful experiences.  If pain is suspected as the ultimate reality,
there must be a lot of anger connected with experiencing it.  By the same token, if pain is assumed
to only come to life's stepchildren, this, too, must create bitterness and rage.  Often, these feelings

Pathwork Guide Lecture No. 253 (An Unedited Lecture)
Page 7 of 9
augment the pain, extend it until the pain can become the medicine it is meant to be.  That is, you
can use it as the guidepost for these other feelings so as to ferret them out and become acutely
conscious of them.  If pain is defended against, even on the deepest possible psychic level, a
tightening comes into existence that prevents healing.  Healing requires a deep and more than
physical relaxation of the entire human system in order to connect with the ever present divine
healing currents that penetrate all that is.  A system that is defended against anything -- be it
common human experience such as pain, suffering, and death, be it one's own feelings of rage and
bitterness about what seems insane to resist and react against -- is in a state of tension and therefore
unable to heal itself.
This state of deep relaxation of body, mind, and the feeling self brings about the attitude I
described at the beginning of this lecture, a state that  may seem impossible ever to attain.  This kind
of equanimity does not express a disregard for earthly pleasure and life in the body.  But it no longer
fears their absence.  This state does not rush into death and pain, but feels an inner peace because
the glimpses of reality follow more quickly in succession.  This is so because the person has begun
to closely observe reactions to the fears and desires in regard to life and death, pleasure and pain.
And as these observations become more honest, more clearly defined, more detached, less involved
(that which is being observed is not being confused with who the person is as a whole), a new state
of mind, the unitive state of mind, is automatically and inexorably, if ever so slowly, ushered in.
So, my beloved friends, try to think about all this and begin a new outlook and direction,
wherever possible, on your individual paths.  It will facilitate much and it will ready you for the great
fusion that must ultimately come about for each created being, a fusion that no longer knows the
pain and separateness of the dualistic state of mind.
As you search in this direction given you here, you will also find, once again, a "reverse unity"
which, in its own way, will help you to understand the nature of your mind steeped in dualistic
confusions.  Every so often you believe you fear one end of the spectrum and strive and desire for
the opposite end of it.  But as you confront your real feelings, as opposed to your illusion about
yourself, you find that you fear the apparently desired end (at least on one important level of
intentionality) perhaps every bit as much as that which you consciously fear.  So you realize the
"unity" of fear.  Life is feared as much as death; pain as much as pleasure; failure as much as success.
Out of this "reverse unity" a real unity can grow, when you comprehend the nature of the fear at
both ends of the spectrum.  As you get in touch with both fears, you have inadvertently attained a
certain measure of equanimity.  The strain automatically relaxes and you are then confronted with
the issue of faith.  There comes the point on your path when it is a question of just that.  Do you
wish to be open to your surrounding universe and look at it from the point of view of justifying
faith?  Do you only see, perhaps wish to see in anger and bitterness, the out -of-context fragments of
life that seem to imply cruelty and meaninglessness?  This question may occupy you over years of
serious and beautiful struggle, the most noble struggle in the human soul.  But the time must come
when inner, deeply experienced answers will come.
Negation of truth, beauty, love, and the meaning of creation always stems from bitterness,
fear, and anger.  This can only open more vistas that justify this negation and hide the vistas that
harbor the most realistically grounded affirmation of all opposites: of life and death, pleasure and
pain, light and darkness.

Pathwork Guide Lecture No. 253 (An Unedited Lecture)
Page 8 of 9
When you can maintain this vision, even while in pain; when you can know that God does it
right, even while you face the great unknown  (however near or far it may be), your mind will be
stilled.  It will have ceased the struggle that attempts to "find out" of the pain of duality but in fact
only draws the net tighter by the very nature of the struggle itself.  The tense movement away from
one and toward another "goal" will cease, and the underlying unity of all life will be experienced.
This ceasing of a particular level and type of struggle must not be confused with apathy,
passivity, lack of initiative, and so on.  You know very well how important your committed active
effort is, how noble your struggle, as I point out again and again.  Struggle on one level, in a certain
way, is necessary; it is the inevitable prerequisite for plowing through the mazes of the mind.
Struggle on another level, in another way, is the movement that ripples the water and prevents the
peace that flows from the Most Holy.
Struggle is another of the dualities that exist in your world.  Many spiritual movements totally
negate its necessity and advocate detachment, not only from worldly matters, but from all striving.
They are completely correct in that they know what I attempt to make you see here.  They think of
that level where fear and desire annihilate unity and trap the mind into deeper illusions of the world.
But they do not connect with that level of the personality that needs to strive and struggle.  They
ignore that there exists a healthy and constructive struggle.  The pitfall of this one -sidedness is that,
through its very one -sidedness, it leads, from a subtle direction, again into more duality and thus
perverts the peace that may occasionally be experienced at first, into a passive standstill.
Then you have those spiritual approaches which advocate the struggle and the work.  They,
too, are correct.  They know the necessity for it and help the followers to summon the energies and
stamina.  But they often ignore that other level where struggle defeats the purpose and only ripples
the waters more stormily.
To you, my friends, I bring the truth of both ends of this particular human split.  Continue
your struggle, and cease all struggle .  Grope for where struggle must continue and where it must
cease.  And you will experience at some time the incomparable peace of no longer fearing what you
do not want and no longer reaching anxiously and strenuously for what you want, because you will
know that all that could ever be desirable is right here, attainable right now, ever present at the tips
of your fingers, and all that you fear and strain away from is nothing but illusion, even though you
may be in the midst of experiencing it.  So you will truly become still and know God.  You will know
God in all that is, in the best and worst, in what you want and what you do not want.  Both are what
your deeper self knows is intensely desirable, much better than what you think you want and not at
all what you fear.
This is but a vague outline for your further path, perhaps a whiff that can be gleaned now.
Even that vague gleaning will prepare you better for your further glorious path, my blessed, beloved
friends.  You all live and move and have your being in the Christ consciousness, in the Christ
principle!

Pathwork Guide Lecture No. 254
An Unedited Lecture
October 18, 1978
SURRENDER
My beloved friends, the light of the Eternal streams as a great blessing to all of you, to all your
endeavors that are sanctified by your commitment to serve God and His magnificent evolutionary
plan.
The hand of God can be recognized in many earthly manifestations.  His presence can be
keenly felt -- and so can it be felt when His presence is being blocked out by man turning away from
Him who is always present.  One of the earthly manifestations in which God's works, divine
creativity, the eternal spirit, can always be seen, is nature.  In nature you cannot help but marvel at
the wisdom and foresight manifest of every smallest detail to protect, sustain and maintain every
species.  The abundance with which all created entities are being provided for, the beauty, the
richness, speak clearly and eloquently that only the greatest of all imaginable minds could have
devised the many systems that maintain life on earth.
It also has become clear to many human beings that the balance is being disturbed through
thoughtless or greedy dispositions.  More awareness has grown in this regard in recent times, and
this is important, of course.
But there is also an aspect in nature that seems contradictory to divine love; an aspect that
seems, in fact cruel.  There exist destructive forces -- storms, floods, earthquakes.  But when seen
from another angle, you will recognize that these manifestations are nothing but the necessary crises
every entity must go through in its process to reestablish inner harmony with divine law.
There is another manifestation in nature fall into a different category.  It is the fact that one
species of animal can often only maintain its life at the expense of another species.  Thus you have
predators and victims.  Although the victims are always equipped with the best measures of defense
so as to give them what you may call a "sporting chance," on the whole, one species often serves the
maintenance of the other.  And all of these various conditions contribute to maintain an overall
balance.  This manifestation of one animal killing another for its nourishment may appear a cruel
measure and appears to deny God's presence in this regard.  Although animals can never indulge in
the useless cruelty and destructiveness that human beings are capable of (precisely due to man's
higher evolved consciousness that can always channel itself into either direction of good or evil), it
does seem -- and in a sense, is -- tragic that a n animal needs to endure panic and pain in order to
serve the total life process.
Now I want you to understand that this manifestation reflects precisely humanity's overall
state of consciousness, which is dualistic.  It is a combination of good and evil.  Man's belief system
contains always this polarity.  Since his total belief system creates the environment, the earth sphere
reflects exactly this polarity.  It can be observed in the most remote manifestations that on the

Pathwork Guide Lecture No. 254 (An Unedited Lecture)
